_comment: The single source of truth for WHICH COMPETITION FORMATS DRAW A KNOCKOUT
BRACKET, shared by both language implementations:
internal/engine/court_validation.go CompetitionDrawsBracket (which scopes
the server's shiaijo-count refusal, via ValidateCompetitionShiaijoCount) and
web-mobile/js/admin_helpers.jsx formatDrawsBracket (which scopes the
console's, via shiaijoCountErrorFor).
THE CONTRACT: the answer follows the DRAW PIPELINE's format switch, not the
UI's idea of which formats are 'playoff-ish'. League and Swiss produce pools
or rounds and never a bracket; mixed builds one after its pools; playoffs and
any UNRECOGNISED value (including a legacy record carrying no format at all)
fall to the pipeline's default branch, which builds a standalone playoffs
bracket. That default is why the unknown-format cases below are true rather
than false, and it is the half a hand-written mirror gets wrong.
WHY THIS TABLE EXISTS: the two implementations run in different processes and
cannot import each other, and the drift is SILENT in both directions. Flip a
format here and forget the console, and it keeps applying the power-of-two
rule to a format the server exempts, disabling Create and Start and printing
a red error for an allocation the server would accept. Flip the console and
forget the server, and the operator is offered a count the draw then refuses.
Neither shows up in either suite unless both read this file.
COVERAGE IS ENFORCED: the Go half asserts that every state.CompFormat*
constant appears below, so adding a format without deciding this question
fails the build rather than defaulting quietly.

cases.why: playoffs is a bracket from the first bout
mixed builds a knockout after its pools, so the rule binds
league is a full round-robin: its shiaijo run in parallel with no blocks to merge
swiss pairs each round afresh and never builds a bracket
a legacy record with no format at all takes the pipeline's default branch
an unrecognised format takes that same default, so it is held to the rule
the match is exact: a format is not league merely by containing it
and it is case-sensitive, matching the stored lowercase wire values
